AI_CheckViability.reason: data/battle_ai_scripts.s:652. Modelled (issue #237) for the three scoreable effects only, and it is the script that actually costs draws in this battle. EFFECT_HIT is absent from the whole if_effect chain (:654-:777), so the script ends immediately with no draw and no score change. AI_CV_AttackDown (:1090-:1110, Growl) is modelled instruction for instruction, including its two conditional 'if_random_less_than 50' rolls: the AI_CV_AttackDown2 roll is reached only once the target's Attack stage has left DEFAULT_STAT_STAGE and dropped to 3 or below, while the AI_CV_AttackDown4 roll fires whenever neither of the target's types is in AI_CV_AttackDown_PhysicalTypeList (:1115-:1121, transcribed with upstream's own Flying/Poison/Ghost omissions intact) -- so an opening Growl against a Grass/Fire/Water starter costs exactly one draw. AI_CV_DefenseDown (:1124-:1134, Leer) is modelled the same way, including the healthy-user/high-stage shortcut that skips its roll entirely, which is why Brendan's Treecko opens one draw cheaper than May's Mudkip. if_hp_more_than/less_than are the truncating '100 * hp / maxHP' percentage (battle_ai_script_commands.c:728), and if_stat_level_* compare the raw 0..12 statStages byte (StatStage::raw_index). NOT modelled: every other if_effect handler in the chain, several of which draw (AI_CV_HighCrit, AI_CV_Sleep, the stat-up family), which is exactly why Battle::new_trainer screens the party's effects up front instead of discovering one mid-battle.

AI_TryToFaint.reason: data/battle_ai_scripts.s:2616. Modelled in full for the three scoreable effects (issue #237), including its one RNG draw. if_can_faint (Cmd_if_can_faint, battle_ai_script_commands.c:1743) is where the kept simulatedRNG values are read: a 0/1-power move returns immediately, otherwise AI_CalcDmg (base_damage with gCritMultiplier and dmgMultiplier both 1) plus TypeCalc's STAB and type rows, scaled by simulatedRNG[movesetIndex]/100 and floored at 1, is compared against the target's CURRENT HP -- so the branch really fires once the player's mon is worn down, taking the +4 that makes the rival stop using Growl and finish the fight. get_how_powerful_move_is (:1174) is modelled including that each other slot's estimate uses THAT slot's own simulatedRNG[checkedMove], and that the considered slot compares against moveDmgs[movesetIndex] (0 for a 0-power move). The only Random() on this script is AI_TryToFaint_DoubleSuperEffective's 'if_random_less_than 80' (:2625), reachable only when the move cannot faint AND reads as AI_EFFECTIVENESS_x4; a Normal move against a single-type starter never is, so this battle never spends it, but the branch is modelled rather than assumed away because a wrong draw count would desynchronise every later roll. InsideOfTruck_EventScript_SetIntroFlags.reason: The gender branch of the truck's exit-tile trigger, ported as its flag/var effect: assets::new_game_flags::TRUCK_INTRO_FLAGS_MALE/_FEMALE (5 setflags each) and TRUCK_INTRO_VARS_MALE/_FEMALE (VAR_LITTLEROOT_INTRO_STATE, VAR_LITTLEROOT_HOUSES_STATE_BRENDAN/_MAY), applied by crate::new_game::apply_truck_intro_flags at new-game init. Upstream this is a coord (trigger) event on all three truck exit tiles gated on VAR_LITTLEROOT_INTRO_STATE == 0 (data/maps/InsideOfTruck/map.json:85-112), so it fires exactly once on the way out of the truck and every real playthrough passes through it before reaching a house; this port skips the truck sequence entirely, so new-game init is the point the skipped flow would have produced the effect -- same 'the effect, without an interpreter' shape as the EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags application beside it. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic now that object-event visibility gates collision and rendering (issue #161): without it a fresh save reaches the player's house with the rival's Poke Ball spawned in the bedroom as an invisible collider and the rival's mother and sibling spawned in the player's own 1F (a duplicated mother plus another undrawn blocker). The two branches are exact Brendan/May mirrors, and a playerGender byte outside MALE/FEMALE applies neither, matching the script's own missing else. As of issue #261, the leading setrespawn HEAL_LOCATION_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_{BRENDANS,MAYS}_HOUSE_2F line IS modelled too -- crate::new_game::default_last_heal_location reproduces its SetLastHealLocationWarp effect (gender-branched, same fallback-to-no-op for an out-of-range gender byte), applied to SaveBlock1::last_heal_location alongside this artifact's own flags/vars at init_save_blocks time; see src/overworld.c#SetLastHealLocationWarp for the full citation. Still not modelled: setdynamicwarp MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN (no dynamic-warp destination state), the lockall/releaseall pair, and setflag FLAG_HIDE_MAP_NAME_POPUP (outside both gender branches; no map-name popup is rendered). The rest of this file -- InsideOfTruck_OnLoad's setmetatile calls, InsideOfTruck_OnResume's STEP_CB_TRUCK step callback, and the moving-box sign -- is untouched: the truck map itself is not bundled.

SecretBase_EventScript_SetDecorationFlag.reason: The 14 setflag FLAG_DECORATION_1..14 commands, ported as their effect: crate::flow::overworld_phase::run_on_transition_map_script applies assets::object_event_flags::DECORATION_FLAGS on entering either bundled player bedroom, the two maps whose own MAP_SCRIPT_ON_TRANSITION calls this script (LittlerootTown_{Brendans,Mays}House_2F/scripts.inc:6-12). Required for correctness, not cosmetics: decoration placeholders invert the usual polarity (an EMPTY slot is the flag-SET state), nothing sets these at new-game time (InitEventData zeroes all flags; EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags never mentions them), and upstream relies purely on ordering -- RunOnTransitionMapScript (overworld.c:860) precedes TrySpawnObjectEvents (overworld.c:2163-2178) -- so without it a fresh save reads all twelve bedroom placeholders as spawned, i.e. as invisible blockers (DoesObjectCollideWithObjectAt consults only active, coordinates and elevation, never the invisible flag, so even MOVEMENT_TYPE_INVISIBLE would still block). Stubbed, not rewritten: no script interpreter runs this, and the maps that call it are a transcribed list rather than a parsed map-script table. Not modelled: the secret-base callers (data/scripts/shared_secret_base.inc:12-16) and flags 13/14's secret-base-only slots.

Deliberately NOT modelled, each an honest scope cut (crates/xtask/src/extract/midi/compile.rs's module docs): the note-duration LUT quantization path (only reachable without -E, which mus_title never omits), -X/48-clocks-per-beat (this schema has no ticks-per-quarter-note field to record it), tools/mid2agb's WAIT-opcode-legal-value bucketing and whole-note pattern-compression bookkeeping (SplitTime/WholeNoteMark/PATT/PEND -- on-disk artifacts with zero audible effect), operand elision (EOT's omitted key, compressed note/velocity mnemonics -- this compiler's stream is always fully explicit), and the MEMACC controller family (0x0C/0x0D/0x0E/0x0F/0x10/0x11 -- mus_title carries zero, confirmed against a locally built tools/mid2agb oracle; the schema's one canonical MEMACC user, mus_vs_trainer, is a different song out of this issue's scope). DoesObjectCollideWithObjectAt.reason: COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT: the destination-tile occupancy test, re-implemented as PlayerState::step's third and last collision check (after the grid collision bits and the elevation mismatch, matching GetCollisionAtCoords' own test order), via engine::overworld::object_event::visible_object_event_at. AreElevationsCompatible is the same either-side-ELEVATION_TRANSITION wildcard predicate MapRuntime::object_events_at already applies. Narrowed, all invisible in this slice: upstream's curObject != objectEvent self-skip has no counterpart (the player is a PlayerState, never an entry in the map's own object_events list), upstream's second previousCoords term is unobservable while every object event is stationary, and a connection-crossing step does not run the test at all because ConnectedMapData exposes no neighbouring-map event data.

GetObjectEventIdByPosition.reason: Position-plus-elevation-wildcard object-event scan rewritten as MapRuntime::object_events_at (issue #108/#149/#161). ObjectEventDoesElevationMatch's rule (either side's ELEVATION_TRANSITION is a wildcard) is folded into that method's own filter predicate. It returns an *iterator* over every match on the tile, not a single hit, because upstream only ever scans spawned object events (a set hide flag prevents the spawn -- see TrySpawnObjectEventTemplate below) while this port scans templates: the hide-flag filter therefore has to run inside the scan, which engine::overworld::object_event::visible_object_event_at does. Both consumers -- the player-interaction lookup (facing_object_event) and the player's own movement collision (PlayerState::step's COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT check) -- go through that one composed search, so they can never disagree about which object event occupies a tile. Templates really do stack per tile with independent flags (the Birch lab's three starter balls at (6, 8)). Known narrowing: the scan matches the template's map.json elevation, whereas upstream compares currentElevation, which ObjectEventUpdateElevation overwrites from the ground on the spawn frame (event_object_movement.c:1758-1770, :8089); the two agree for every bundled map and cannot diverge while all object events are stationary, but this now governs movement as well as interaction.

IsMetatileDirectionallyImpassable.reason: Rewritten as engine::overworld::collision::directionally_impassable (issue #218), wired into PlayerState::step at GetCollisionAtCoords' own position -- ||'d into the same COLLISION_IMPASSABLE arm as the grid collision bits (:4663), ahead of IsElevationMismatchAt. Both of upstream's function tables are modelled: gOppositeDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs against the tile the mover stands on (same-direction predicate) and gDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs against the destination (opposite-direction predicate), :893-905. The standing tile's behavior is re-read from the grid at the mover's position rather than cached in an objectEvent field, which ObjectEventUpdateMetatileBehaviors (:7428-7432) keeps equal to that same read. NOT modelled: the destination half across a map connection -- ConnectedMapData exposes decoded cells but not the neighbouring map's tileset attribute tables, so a connection landing tile reads as MB_NORMAL (no bundled map places an MB_IMPASSABLE_* tile on a connection edge); and this port only calls it for the player, since NPCs do not move.

ObjectEventUpdateElevation.reason: Current-vs-previous elevation split (issue #218): PlayerState::adopt_elevation reproduces the early-return-on-either-side-ELEVATION_MULTI_LEVEL guard and the unconditional currentElevation adopt / non-transition-only previousElevation adopt, called from both of PlayerState::step's arrival sites (same-map and connection-crossing). previousElevation now exposed as PlayerState::previous_elevation, feeding the player OBJ's elevation-driven render priority.

SetSpritePosToMapCoords.reason: Player-OBJ screen-position derivation: for the player's own object event mapX/mapY == gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos always, collapsing this to a per-frame-constant OAM origin (PLAYER_OBJ_X/PLAYER_OBJ_Y); the camera/BG scrolls instead (viewport::build_tilemaps). Bike pan-ahead (the only thing that would move dx/dy away from 0) is not modelled yet -- deferred, still in v1 scope.

TrySpawnObjectEventTemplate.reason: The hide-flag gate (!FlagGet(template->flagId)) is reproduced at query time -- object_event_is_visible, and the visible_object_events/visible_object_event_at searches built on it, treat a hidden object event as absent everywhere (rendering, the facing-tile interaction lookup, and movement collision alike), behaviourally identical to it never having been spawned -- rather than by modelling a persistent active-object-event instance list. Because the filter is applied at query time rather than at spawn time, every such search applies it *inside* its scan, so a tile carrying several stacked templates with independent hide flags resolves to the first visible one, exactly as scanning a spawned-only gObjectEvents would. Not modelled: the camera-radius spawn/despawn this function and RemoveObjectEventsOutsideView perform (every visible object event is always 'spawned', unconditional on distance from the player), the persistent gObjectEvents slot table, link-player object events, and the Trainer Hill/Battle Pyramid dynamic object-event-count special cases.

TrySpawnObjectEvents.reason: The in-range rectangle that decides whether a template spawns, rewritten as engine::overworld::object_event_is_in_view (issue #161 review): transcribed in upstream's own two coordinate spaces (the window around gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos, each candidate tested as template->{x,y} + MAP_OFFSET), which reduces to player.x - 9 ..= player.x + 10 by player.y - 7 ..= player.y + 9. RemoveObjectEventIfOutsideView spells the same bounds as the despawn test. Consumed by the NPC render path (crate::overworld::npc::oam_entries) only, and load-bearing there rather than an optimization: the GBA OAM y field is 8 bits, so without this gate an object event exactly 16 metatiles away wraps onto the player's own screen row (MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN's unhideable boy at (14, 17) did). Deliberately NOT applied to the collision/interaction path, where it is unobservable -- those only ever query a tile adjacent to the player. The flag-gate half of this function stays recorded under TrySpawnObjectEventTemplate; not modelled here: the camera-radius spawn/despawn lifecycle itself, RemoveObjectEvent, and the Trainer Hill/Battle Pyramid object-count special cases.

UpdateObjectEventElevationAndPriority.reason: sElevationToPriority transcribed as avatar::ELEVATION_TO_PRIORITY / priority_for_elevation, now driving BOTH the player OBJ's OAM priority (from PlayerState::previous_elevation) and every stationary NPC/object event's (from its template elevation, npc::oam_entries) -- replacing the fixed PLAYER_OBJ_PRIORITY both used to draw at. sElevationToSubspriteTableNum (:7733-7735) has no counterpart, and for 16x32 object events it costs nothing: its values index sOamTables_16x32 (object_event_subsprites.h:176-183) entries 1/2/0, which are a single full-size 16x32 subsprite at priority 2, a single full-size 16x32 at priority 1, and the empty table AddSubspritesToOamBuffer copies through as the plain OBJ at oam.priority -- exactly the values sElevationToPriority already gives, so one OBJ at priority_for_elevation's value is pixel-identical. The genuinely multi-piece tables are reached only by SetObjectEventSpriteOamTableForLongGrass (:7690-7705, table nums 4/5), an unported ground effect. Stubbed, not rewritten: the fixedPriority branch is NOT modelled -- the Rust render path unconditionally derives an elevation priority, so a fixed-priority object event would diverge once one is bundled. Also NOT modelled: subpriority (sElevationToSubpriority/SetObjectSubpriorityByElevation) and the grid re-derivation of an object's previousElevation on its first DoGroundEffects_OnSpawn pass (SceneSprites has no layout grid; see npc::oam_entries' comment for the one bundled object it would move, an unbound doll). This function is also where a freshly spawned object event's ELEVATION_TRANSITION landing sentinel gets resolved (first statement past the fixedPriority early-return): its ObjectEventUpdateElevation(objEvent) call (event_object_movement.c:7742) runs from DoGroundEffects_OnSpawn (:4931, gated by triggerGroundEffectsOnMove = TRUE, set for every fresh spawn by InitObjectEventStateFromTemplate at :1301) on the spawn frame itself, before input unlocks -- not deferred to the object's first subsequent step. engine::overworld::warp_destination_position (crates/engine/src/overworld/warp.rs) is this port's faithful model of that same spawn-frame resolution for OverworldPhase::warp_to's resolved-warp-event landings (issue #297).

gDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs.reason: See gOppositeDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs: same fold into collision::directionally_impassable. This table pairs each direction with the OPPOSITE predicate (north -> IsSouthBlocked, west -> IsEastBlocked, ...) and is applied to MapGridGetMetatileBehaviorAt(x, y), the destination tile (:4718).

gInitialMovementTypeFacingDirections.reason: Transcribed in full: engine::overworld::initial_facing_direction covers all 81 MOVEMENT_TYPE_* entries, mirroring InitObjectEventStateFromTemplate's initial-spawn-facing table. This port has no per-object movement-type task simulation yet (this port so far: stationary + look-around only), so this is also the facing an object renders at forever, not just at spawn -- a MOVEMENT_TYPE_LOOK_AROUND/WANDER_* object's own random-turn cycling (MovementType_LookAround et al.) is not modelled.

gOppositeDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs.reason: The direction-to-predicate pairing is folded into collision::directionally_impassable's match rather than transcribed as a function-pointer array (no-verbatim; Rust has no DIR_* index to key on -- Direction is an enum). This table pairs each direction with its own predicate and is applied to objectEvent->currentMetatileBehavior, the tile the mover stands on (:4717); its sibling gDirectionBlockedMetatileFuncs supplies the opposite pairing for the destination. Both pairings are pinned by their own tests in collision.rs, since swapping them is the failure mode this table's name invites.

CameraUpdate.reason: Per-frame gFieldCamera pixel-offset accumulator (movementSpeedX/Y ramping gTotalCameraPixelOffsetX/Y by 1px/frame toward a full metatile) collapsed to the analytic viewport::camera_lag_px, which derives the same net signed pixel lag directly from PlayerState::step_progress/WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE rather than replicating the accumulator. Related to, but a strictly bigger step than, SetSpritePosToMapCoords' own ledger entry: that one collapses a compile-time *constant* (the player's own mapX - gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos.x is identically 0), while this collapses a per-frame *accumulator* into a closed form -- and only up to the constant term already folded into PLAYER_OBJ_X/Y, so it equals upstream's own value on frame-to-frame differences rather than absolutely (see camera_lag_px's docs). Issue #217 (I-3): this shared value is what fixed the NPC-camera desync bug (a stationary NPC snapping to its destination tile at step start while the BG still lagged smoothly behind), used identically by build_tilemaps' BG scroll and npc::oam_entries' NPC placement. UpdateObjectEventsForCameraUpdate's own spawn/despawn side effect (TrySpawnObjectEvents/RemoveObjectEventsOutsideView at camera tile boundaries) stays under its own existing event_object_movement.c ledger entries -- not re-claimed here.

DrawMetatile.reason: Per-METATILE_LAYER_TYPE bottom/middle/top BG-layer routing of a metatile's 8 raw tile entries, ported into viewport::route_layers; the NORMAL case's 'garbage' bottom-layer write is a documented fidelity delta (drawn transparent instead, since it is implementation-undefined and never reaches the screen behind the always-opaque middle layer in the common case).

DrawMetatileAt.reason: Per-position metatile-id lookup plus primary/secondary tileset dispatch (NUM_METATILES_IN_PRIMARY threshold) feeding DrawMetatile, ported into viewport::metatile_layers/cell_at.

UpdateCameraPanning.reason: gSpriteCoordOffsetX/Y's per-frame derivation from the camera's own pixel state, ported as the shared viewport::camera_lag_px this port's two camera-driven consumers both read (issue #217, I-3): build_tilemaps subtracts it from the BG scroll (mirroring gSpriteCoordOffsetX/Y being the camera-locked complement to the world-locked BG scroll) and npc::oam_entries adds it to every stationary NPC's placement (mirroring UpdateOamCoords -- see src/sprite.c#UpdateOamCoords). sHorizontalCameraPan/sVerticalCameraPan's bike pan-ahead terms are not modelled yet (no bike in this port yet) -- deferred, still in v1 scope.

CheckStandardWildEncounter.reason: field_control_avatar.c:668-686. Fully modelled as WildEncounterState::check_standard_wild_encounter, including the four-step post-transition immunity window (which returns before StandardWildEncounter is reached, so it is invisible to the RNG stream, not merely to the player), the reset on a fired encounter (:679), and sPrevMetatileBehavior being updated on every step including suppressed ones (:673). Stubbed rather than rewritten because its caller's gating is only partially ported: FieldGetPlayerInput sets input->checkStandardWildEncounter at every T_TILE_CENTER regardless of runningState (:117-120), while OverworldPhase::step ties the roll to a landing a step actually committed. The two differ only on a frame where the player reaches a tile centre without having moved, which this port's PlayerState cannot produce for any bundled map. The forced-movement gate around that flag (:95, MetatileBehavior_IsForcedMovementTile) is not modelled either, because forced movement itself is not modelled yet -- deferred, still in v1 scope.

GetInFrontOfPlayerPosition.reason: The facing-tile position (GetXYCoordsOneStepInFrontOfPlayer, player position + facing delta) plus the own-tile-elevation wildcard rule rewritten as engine::overworld::facing_object_event's query-elevation derivation: the player's own grid cell's elevation, unless it is itself ELEVATION_TRANSITION, in which case the query elevation is the wildcard too.

IsArrowWarpMetatileBehavior.reason: engine::overworld::warp::is_arrow_warp_trigger: dispatches by direction to metatile_behavior::is_{north,south,west,east}_arrow_warp exactly as upstream's sArrowWarpMetatileBehaviorChecks table does (field_player_avatar.c:226-232). Issue #174.

RestartWildEncounterImmunitySteps.reason: field_control_avatar.c:662-666. Fully modelled as WildEncounterState::restart_immunity_steps -- zeroes the step counter only, deliberately leaving sPrevMetatileBehavior alone as upstream does (they are two separate statics). Wired at this port's counterparts of upstream's map-load call sites: OverworldPhase::warp_to (LoadMapFromWarp, overworld.c:850) and OverworldPhase::cross_connection (LoadMapFromCameraTransition, overworld.c:800 -- the piece issue #177 explicitly deferred to this slice). The battle-start call sites (battle_setup.c:370, :941) are covered by CheckStandardWildEncounter's own reset on a fired encounter, which upstream also performs (:679).

TryArrowWarp.reason: GetWarpEventAtMapPosition + IsArrowWarpMetatileBehavior + SetupWarp/DoWarp's warp-resolution shape absorbed into engine::overworld::warp::trigger_arrow_warp, a separate entry point from the door-shaped trigger_door_warp precisely because the two are gated differently upstream. Called from crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/step.rs's OverworldPhase::step as a per-frame poll, upstream's own gating: the direction currently held must equal the direction the player currently faces (input->heldDirection && input->dpadDirection == playerDirection, field_control_avatar.c:164-168), evaluated at the tile the player is standing on, independent of tookStep -- so it fires both for a step taken onto an arrow tile while still holding its direction and for a turn in place while already standing on one. The only added gate is that the player be at rest between steps, which is this port's counterpart to the T_TILE_CENTER/T_NOT_MOVING test that sets heldDirection upstream in the first place (:95-112). Issue #174 (the Brendan's-house exit doormat, MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_BRENDANS_HOUSE_1F warp #1 at (8, 8)). Issue #194 corrected the frame ordering against ProcessPlayerFieldInput (overworld.c:1444-1455), which runs this check *before* PlayerStep and skips the step outright when it fires: OverworldPhase::step now re-evaluates this same pre-movement gate ahead of its own movement call and, when it already fires, skips movement for the frame entirely instead of running it and polling afterward -- so a legal, walkable step in the arrow direction warps rather than stepping (previously a permanent no-warp, unreachable on bundled data since every arrow tile's own direction is impassable there, and pinned now by a synthetic scene in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests.rs). The door-shaped path is unaffected: its own tookStep-style gate inherently needs the step to have already landed, so it still runs after movement. Not modelled: StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState's pre-warp avatar snapshot, and SetupWarp's escape-warp/Trainer Hill bookkeeping.

TryStartInteractionScript.reason: OverworldPhase::step's A-press handling covers only the object-event branch of GetInteractionScript (GetInteractedObjectEventScript, via engine::overworld::facing_object_event), routed to a NpcDialog through crate::overworld::npc_scripts::script_text's own small, hardcoded msgbox-style script-text table (issue's own DoD: 'a direct msgbox-style script subset is enough'). Not modelled: GetInteractedBackgroundEventScript/GetInteractedMetatileScript/GetInteractedWaterScript's fallback chain (sign posts, counters, water-adjacent interactions), GetInteractedLinkPlayerScript, RamScript, and the interaction sound effect (PlaySE(SE_SELECT)). A found-but-unrecognized-script object event (including the literal NULL/'0x0' sentinel) is selected but opens no dialog, matching upstream's own NULL-script no-op.

CheckForPlayerAvatarCollision.reason: Destination-tile collision check re-implemented via MapRuntime::metatile_cell plus collision.rs's Collision/elevation_mismatch, and (issue #161, I-3 lane) the object-event occupancy test -- the grid collision-bit, elevation-mismatch and object-event cases, applied in GetCollisionAtCoords' own order. Still not modelled (deferred, all still in v1 scope): the ledge, boulder-push, rotating-gate and acro-bike sub-checks, plus IsCoordOutsideObjectEventMovementRange (never constrains the player), IsMetatileDirectionallyImpassable and CanCameraMoveInDirection.

CheckMovementInputNotOnBike.reason: NOT_MOVING/TURN_DIRECTION/MOVING classification re-implemented as PlayerState::step's running-state branch, including the exact turn-vs-step rule (direction change only turns when not already mid-movement)

GetPlayerMovementDirection.reason: Folded into the same PlayerState::facing field as GetPlayerFacingDirection: upstream's facingDirection/movementDirection only diverge under facingDirectionLocked (bike wheelies/slides), which this port does not model yet, so it has no way to tell them apart and no need to; revisit the fold when the bike lands (deferred, still in v1 scope)

FillConnection.reason: The shared rectangular-copy helper collapses into connected_cell_at's own LayoutGrid::cell_at lookup once its four callers' own coordinate math is inlined per-direction; this port resolves one cell on demand rather than copying a whole strip into a backing buffer, but only within the exact extents that buffer covers (viewport::within_backup_map_band).

FillEastConnection.reason: East-edge offset math (target_x = x - width, target_y = y - offset) re-implemented in connected_cell_at, bounded to gBackupMapLayout's own east cover -- upstream's MAP_OFFSET + 1 copy width (a fixed-buffer sizing artifact of MAP_OFFSET_W's odd total, include/fieldmap.h:19) reproduced as layout-local x <= width + 7 (issue #253).

FillNorthConnection.reason: North-edge offset math (target_x = x - offset, target_y = connected_height + y) re-implemented in connected_cell_at, bounded to gBackupMapLayout's own MAP_OFFSET rows north of the layout (layout-local y >= -7), same shape as FillSouthConnection's own ledger entry.

GetHealLocation.reason: heal_location.c: GetHealLocation(u32 index) indexes the full sHealLocations table (src/data/heal_locations.json, every HEAL_LOCATION_* id in the game -- Pokemon Centers, home beds, Battle Frontier respawns, etc). This port has no general assets::HealLocation lookup: only the two entries new-game init actually needs are transcribed as fixed constants (crate::new_game::DEFAULT_HEAL_LOCATION_MAP_GROUP/_MALE_MAP_NUM/_FEMALE_MAP_NUM/_X/_Y, cross-checked against src/data/heal_locations.json's own HEAL_LOCATION_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_BRENDANS_HOUSE_2F/_MAYS_HOUSE_2F entries by crate::new_game::tests::default_heal_locations_match_the_generated_map_header_positions). This file's two reverse lookups, GetHealLocationIndexByMap (heal_location.c:7-17) and GetHealLocationByMap (:19-27), are likewise not modelled -- and cost nothing to skip: neither has a single caller anywhere upstream (both are declared in include/heal_location.h:12-13, and the only reference to either in the tree is GetHealLocationByMap's own call to GetHealLocationIndexByMap). The one place upstream reads lastHealLocation back by map does it without them: ResetHealLocationFromDewford (src/field_specials.c:3880-3885) compares gSaveBlock1Ptr->lastHealLocation.mapGroup/.mapNum against MAP_DEWFORD_TOWN directly and calls SetLastHealLocationWarp(HEAL_LOCATION_PETALBURG_CITY) -- a softlock guard for a player who respawns on Dewford with no way off the island, not a table lookup, and not modelled here either (no Dewford, no Petalburg heal location bundled). A future slice adding a Pokemon Center heal flow (setrespawn's other real call sites) is what would give this file a real table-backed home instead of two named constants.

CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave.reason: CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave/FromSave (:196-206) and the SavePlayerParty/LoadPlayerParty pair they wrap (:160-178) are OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save/_from_save, called around every start-menu save and on every continue (issue #232). gPlayerParty is this port's single OverworldPhase::party_lead, encoded to and from SaveBlock1::playerParty[0] by pokeemerald_rs::party -- species, level, accumulated experience (MON_DATA_EXP, carried since issue #237 made in-battle experience real state rather than a function of the level), personality/nature, the six IVs, the moveset with per-slot PP, the packed ppBonuses byte (issue #304 -- written back byte-exact, including bits for slots the moveset does not fill, so a load/save cycle can no longer strip a save's PP Ups; pinned by pp_ups_survive_the_round_trip_byte_for_byte and pp_bonus_bits_for_unknown_slots_are_not_stripped in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests.rs), current HP and the OT id all round-trip, so a continued session fights the mon that was saved. NOT modelled on the party side: EVs (battle::BattlePokemon carries none), held item, contest condition, pokerus, met location/level/game, poke ball, OT gender, ribbons, nickname, OT name, language, markings and non-volatile status -- each written as CreateMon's own zero/MAIL_NONE default rather than an invented value (crate::party's module docs carry the list).

SaveObjectEvents.reason: SaveObjectEvents/LoadObjectEvents (:180-194) copy all OBJECT_EVENTS_COUNT entries of gObjectEvents in and out of SaveBlock1::objectEvents. This port models one field of one entry: objectEvents[OBJ_EVENT_ID_PLAYER].facingDirection, as engine::save::SavedObjectEvent at its real offset (0xA30 + 0x18), written by OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save and read back on continue (issue #232). That is the only part of the array a continue observably restores here -- SpawnObjectEventsOnReturnToField respawns the player from it (event_object_movement.c:1715-1726) -- and it removes the DIR_SOUTH stand-in issue #214 recorded. NOT modelled: the other 0x23 bytes of the player's entry (sprite ids, ground-effect and movement bitfields, coordinate history, metatile-behaviour history, movementActionId) and every non-player entry, because this workspace models no object-event system to hold them; a save block whose byte is DIR_NONE still falls back to GetAdjustedInitialDirection.

clear_sav.reason: ClearSav1/ClearSav2's zero-the-blocks-when-a-new-game-starts effect is modelled by SaveStore::clear_base, applied on every write of a new-game session (#230 review; #232 review round two). Upstream settles a new game's RAM once -- NewGameInitData memsets gSaveBlock1 via ClearSav1 (new_game.c:160, load_save.c:64-67, which also covers ResetGameStats's gSaveBlock1Ptr->gameStats) and resets gSaveBlock2's deferred state field by field (encryption key :155, ResetPokedex, PlayTimeCounter_Reset), with Sav2_ClearSetDefault -> ClearSav2 on top when the boot load found nothing usable (intro.c:1155-1156) -- and HandleSavingData then writes a whole slot out of that RAM (save.c:736-739) on every save of the session. This port defers unmodelled bytes to the image on disk, so it re-applies the reset per write, and the clear_base input is a property of the *session* (OverworldPhase::new_game_session, read at the store call as game_save::SaveLineage), never of the save mode: keying it off the save type left a new-game session's SAVE_NORMAL retry -- the arm a cleared gDifferentSaveFile produces after a failed overwrite -- writing the replaced trainer's deferred bytes back out. NOT modelled: the RAM struct pointers/shuffling (SetSaveBlocksPointers, MoveSaveBlocks_ResetHeap) and the checksum globals; and the gSaveBlock2 bytes NewGameInitData never writes for a new game started over an *intact* save -- SetDefaultOptions runs only from the empty/corrupt-boot Sav2_ClearSetDefault, so the option bytes (and e.g. localTimeOffset) survive in RAM upstream and are written back out, whereas clear_base drops them with the rest of the deferred payload.

MidiKeyToFreq.reason: MidiKeyToFreq + umul3232H32 re-implemented behaviourally as pitch::midi_key_to_freq/umul3232_hi (S-3 slice 1).

TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX.reason: The CGB-side use of TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX: Emerald's 8-bit-DAC frequency rounding for a fixed-rate square/wave channel, (freq_reg + 1) & 0x7fe (m4a.c:1184-1202, under the 8-bit DAC configuration selected at m4a.c:70-81), reimplemented as cgb_voice::cgb_dac_correct, applied at note-on (before the oscillator and, on channel 1, the sweep unit's shadow frequency initialize) and again on every mid-note pitch re-run (CgbVoice::set_track_pitch). The flag is threaded from the instrument through loading and playback (PR #276). The DirectSound-side use of the same flag lives on src/m4a_1.s#TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX (Voice::fixed_rate).

TrkVolPitSet.reason: TrkVolPitSet vol/pan+pitch resolution re-implemented as sequencer::track_volume/track_pitch (S-3 slice 1); slice 2 extends both with the MOD/MODT modM folding (amplitude/pan/pitch vibrato).

m4aMPlayFadeOut.reason: m4aMPlayFadeOut/MPlayFadeOut's seeding (m4a.c:58-65, :202) and FadeOutBody's per-frame ramp (m4a.c:692-762, fade-out arm only) reimplemented as MusicPlayer::fade_out and the private FadeOut state: fadeOC/fadeOI/fadeOV with the same 4-per-step drop every 'speed' frames (m4a.c:700, :715) and the same terminal stop-all-tracks state (m4a.c:717-744), stepped once per rendered frame from App::advance_music for the title screen's FadeOutBGM(4) (title_screen.c:784). Covers only this fade-out arm at that one call site. Divergence: upstream applies the resulting volX per track inside TrkVolPitSet (m4a.c:756, :772), upstream of the reverb feedback loop; audio::Sequencer exposes no per-track volume knob, so the same volX/64 gain is applied to the already-mixed f32 frame instead -- identical schedule, step size and duration, differing only in per-channel integer rounding and in fading the reverb tail on its way out. FADE_IN (m4aMPlayFadeIn, m4a.c:219-227) and TEMPORARY_FADE (m4aMPlayFadeOutTemporarily, m4a.c:207) are NOT implemented and stay pending on src/m4a.c.

m4aSongNumStart.reason: App::new/App::boot's title-screen path starts MUS_TITLE (m4aSongNumStart(MUS_TITLE), title_screen.c:661) via MusicPlayer::start_from_pack, frame-driven from App::step for as long as the title scene is active (issue #185, Discussion #227). TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX.reason: SoundMainRAM's fixed-rate DirectSound branch (m4a_1.s:498: tst TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX; movne r8, 0x800000 forces a 1:1 phase step) reimplemented as Voice::fixed_rate forcing the phase step to pitch::FRAC_ONE, which also reproduces the branch's un-interpolated raw-sample reads as a side effect (S-3 slice 3). The separate CGB-side use of the flag (m4a.c:1184-1202 8-bit-DAC frequency rounding) is implemented too, recorded on src/m4a.c#TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX (cgb_voice::cgb_dac_correct, PR #276).

ply_note.reason: ply_note (m4a_1.s:1538) key-split (TONEDATA_TYPE_SPL) / rhythm (TONEDATA_TYPE_RHY) child resolution, the TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX dispatch bypass, and the pseudoEchoVolume/Length note-on snapshot are reimplemented as sequencer::resolve_instrument + note_on (S-3 slice 3). SeedRngAndSetTrainerId.reason: main.c:208-214. Upstream reseeds gRngValue from the TM1CNT_L hardware timer at new-game time (SeedRng(REG_TM1CNT_L)) and stores that same timer value as sTrainerId, the GetGeneratedTrainerIdLower source InitPlayerTrainerId ORs in; retail compiles the boot-time SeedRngWithRtc call out (:229-236 is #ifdef BUGFIX), so gRngValue stays 0 until this runs. NOT modelled: no timer register exists in this port, so new_game::NEW_GAME_RNG_SEED (0, upstream's real pre-seed boot state) stands in and a fresh run is deterministic where retail is not -- deliberate, to keep the headless xtask e2e lanes reproducible (flow::overworld_phase's rng field docs, PR #207). WaitForVBlank.reason: WaitForVBlank's fixed-cadence wait re-implemented as FramePacer::tick, targeting the GBA's real ~59.7275Hz refresh (280896 cycles / 16.777216MHz, per src/m4a.c's own comments) instead of a rounded 60Hz, with hardware-faithful catch-up: it always waits for the next upcoming vblank boundary, never queues up missed frames. Built on an injectable Instant seam so cadence/drift math is unit-tested without sleeping. Rest of main.c (unrelated main-loop plumbing) stays pending.

CalculatePPWithBonus.reason: pokemon.c:4650-:4654, plus the gPPUpGetMask/gPPUpClearMask tables it reads (:1857-:1866). Fully modelled (issue #304) as battle::pokemon::pp_bonuses: PpBonuses is upstream's packed ppBonuses byte (two bits per move slot, struct PokemonSubstruct0::ppBonuses at include/pokemon.h:104 and struct BattlePokemon::ppBonuses at :288) as an owned type, and calculate_pp_with_bonus is basePP + ((basePP * 20 * ppUps) / 100) with upstream's single trailing truncation rather than a per-Up one. BattlePokemon carries the byte whole (not a per-slot field) so the save round trip is byte-exact, including bits belonging to a slot the moveset does not fill; PpBonuses::get is the (gPPUpGetMask[i] & bonuses) >> (2 * i) read and PpBonuses::cleared is gPPUpClearMask's write. Every one of the 256 bytes is accepted -- two-bit fields cannot overflow, so there is nothing to reject. BattlePokemon::max_pp is the per-slot application: it is what HealPlayerParty restores to and what deduct_pp counts down from. The arithmetic runs in u32 and saturates back to u8 where C would wrap, unreachable for real data (the largest gBattleMoves pp is 40, giving 64 fully upgraded). NOT modelled: applying a PP Up at all -- ITEM4_PP_UP's gPPUpAddValues path (:4958-:4972) and the Max Elixir-style :5256-:5264 case need an item-use path this port does not have, so a nonzero byte can only arrive from a save file today.

MonTryLearningNewMove.reason: pokemon.c's level-up move learning (MonTryLearningNewMove, :3014-:3044, and GiveMoveToMon/GiveMoveToBoxMon, :2934-:2955), reached in-battle from Cmd_getexp via BattleScript_LevelUp -> Cmd_handlelearnnewmove (battle_script_commands.c:5360) and in the overworld from the daycare/evolution paths (still not modelled -- see below). As of issue #252, BattlePokemon::apply_experience (crates/battle/src/pokemon.rs, private helper learn_crossed_level_moves) walks every level crossed by a single apply_experience call, in ascending order, and offers each of that level's assets::LevelUpLearnsets entries, in table order, to GiveMoveToBoxMon's two outcomes: a move already known is skipped at no slot cost (MON_ALREADY_KNOWS_MOVE, :2951-:2952), and a move with an empty slot is learned into it at its own base PP (:2945-:2949, writes at :2947-:2948). NOT modelled from the replacement path: the yes/no box, the summary-screen move list (ShowSelectMovePokemonSummaryScreen, :5449), every string, and IsHMMove2's refusal to overwrite an HM slot (:5471-:5475) -- no path in this port can put an HM in a slot, so a refusal would guard nothing. The rotation/scale-to-matrix computation (ObjAffineSet/SetOamMatrix trig side) is not modelled — only matrix selection and consumption are. Windows/blending/mosaic remain out of scope (issue #98).

oam_admission.reason: Not a port of any pokeemerald src/sprite.c function -- pokeemerald itself assumes unlimited per-scanline OAM processing and never models the GBA's fixed OBJ cycle budget. Filed here (alongside affine_oam/oam_mosaic) as the sprite renderer's third mgba-verified hardware-timing artifact: OamAdmission::for_scanline (crate::oam_budget) ports the GBA PPU's real per-scanline OAM admission -- a fixed cycle budget (mgba/include/mgba/internal/gba/video.h:36-37: OBJ_LENGTH=1210 normally, OBJ_HBLANK_FREE_LENGTH=954 when DISPCNT's HBlank-interval-free bit is set, mgba/src/gba/renderers/video-software.c:623) that caps OAM traversal at 128 physical entries (mgba/src/gba/renderers/common.c:13) and drops late sprites/OBJWIN masks once exhausted. sprite_list_cost ports mgba's OAM clean pass (common.c:18-45): an entry that is disabled (common.c:18) or lies entirely off the left edge, x + width < 0 (common.c:34-36 for a regular entry; common.c:43-45, which tests the raw 9-bit X field, rejects an affine one on the same condition), never enters the sprite list at all -- it is neither drawn nor charged its own cost, only the traversal its index contributes. Costs are mgba's two unclipped formulas (common.c:24-39), taken over the entry's bounding-box width (already doubled for AffineDoubleSize per common.c:26): affine 8 + width * 2 then += x when x < 0; regular width - 2 then += x >> 1 when x < 0 (C's arithmetic shift, which Rust's i32 >> reproduces). mgba never clips width to the on-screen part, and the two kinds fall off at different rates: a 64-wide entry costs 62 (regular) / 136 (affine) at x=0, 46 / 104 at x=-32, 30 / 72 at x=-64. The walk itself is video-software.c:1029-1064's charge-then-check ordering: traversal is 2 * (index - lastIndex) with lastIndex starting at 0, so OAM index 0's traversal is free and every later slot costs 2; the charge lands before the exhaustion test; that test is remaining <= 0, not < 0; an off-scanline entry is skipped only after both (video-software.c:1040-1042); and an admitted entry's own cost is deducted only after processing (video-software.c:1064), so a sprite whose own cost crosses zero is still drawn and only the next slot's traversal stops the rest. common.c:43-45's rejection of entries entirely off the *right* edge (x >= 240 -- the raw 9-bit X band 240..=255, which decodes to no visible pixel) is modelled the same way: such a slot retains only the walk's traversal cost and cannot drain the per-scanline budget or displace a later visible sprite (oam_budget.rs's right-edge tests); the case is reachable, snow weather parks wrapped flakes near x = 242 (src/field_weather_effect.c:970). SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel and SpriteLayer::objwin_mask (sprite.rs) both gate their entry iteration through this single admission stage -- reading it out of one per-scanline cache slot (SpriteLayer::with_admission), which both keeps the walk to once per scanline rather than once per pixel per path and makes it structurally impossible for visible resolution and OBJWIN masking to disagree about which entries a scanline exhausted. SpriteLayer::with_hblank_free_interval threads DISPCNT's HBlank-interval-free bit in from the caller -- pokeemerald sets that bit unconditionally in the overworld's DISPCNT setup (src/overworld.c:2122-2123; that file is still ledger-pending overall and this bit is not yet its own tracked artifact), so a future caller wiring live DISPCNT state through gets the reduced 954-cycle budget for free. Issue #329 (S-2).
